subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Cultural Variation in Fairness
description: A fast breakdown of Cultural Variation in Fairness for builders.

hook.text: In the ultimatum game, Americans offer 45%. The Machiguenga of Peru offer 15%. Same game, radically different norms.

buildup.text: Henrich ran the ultimatum game across 15 small-scale societies. Offers ranged from 15% to 58%. Culture shapes fairness.

discovery.text: Societies with more market integration made fairer offers. Trade experience teaches equal exchange as a norm.

twist.text: The Lamelara whale hunters gave more than 50%. Their survival depends on sharing. Ecology shapes economic norms.

climax.text: Fairness is not a universal instinct with a fixed setting. It is shaped by culture, ecology, and economic experience.

punchline.text: Fairness is universal. What counts as fair is not.

quiz.question: What did Henrich's cross-cultural ultimatum game studies show?
options: Market integration correlates with fairer offers
No culture shows fairness in economic games
